$comment: Twelve events across the six categories and every status the demo needs to show: six finished (attendance, check-ins and XP), one happening right now (the scan target), three upcoming and approved (the register target), one awaiting an adviser, one rejected with a reason.
$dates: startsInDays is relative to the moment the seed runs; startsAtHour is the hour of the school day. The one event carrying happeningNow started an hour ago, so the scanner always has something live to point at.
$publish: publish_at is derived as one week before the event for anything approved, completed or cancelled, and stays null otherwise. An unapproved event has no publish date and is invisible to learners by policy, not by query.

events.title: Science Investigatory Project Fair
events.description: Thirty projects on the covered court, judged by teachers from three departments.

events.title: Coastal Clean-up Drive

events.$doubleScanned: Scanned once at the main gate and again at the side entrance, on two different tokens. Both check-ins are real rows; the second award is reversed below rather than deleted.

events.title: Club Fair
events.description: All six organizations have tables. Officers are scanning at the entrance.
events.$attendance: Deliberately empty. This is the event the demo scans into, live, in front of the teacher.

events.title: Line-Follower Build Night

events.$approval: Decision is null: the request is sitting in the adviser queue, which is what the approval screen needs in order to have something to show.

events.title: Barangay Hall Outreach
events.description: Afternoon outreach with the barangay youth council.
events.$approval: A rejection always carries a reason. An officer told no without being told why stops submitting (SYSTEM_DESIGN.md section 3.1).

approval.reason: Clashes with the district meet on the same afternoon, and no adviser escort is confirmed for an off-campus activity. Resubmit with a date after the meet and a named escort.

$manualAwards: XP that is not attendance. Every row still names what it was for and who awarded it, because a point nobody can explain is a point nobody believes.

$corrections: The ledger is append-only, so a wrong award is answered by a reversal row citing the original, never by an edit (CLAUDE.md R4). One is seeded because the demo should show the correction path working rather than claim it exists.
